page.text:
The algebra of sets, initiated by George Boole in the mid-nineteenth
century, exhibits a profound structural isomorphism with propositional
logic. Every logical connective possesses an exact set-theoretic
counterpart: disjunction ($\lor$) corresponds to union ($\cup$),
conjunction ($\land$) corresponds to intersection ($\cap$), and negation
($\neg$) corresponds to relative complement or set difference
($\setminus$).

Through these operations, the power set $\mathcal{P}(U)$ of any ambient
set is endowed with the structure of a complete Boolean algebra,
providing the computational engine for combinatorics, measure theory,
topology, and probability.
